title: Message
description:
Top-level JSON-RPC 2.0 envelope.

Either side of a session may send any of the three variants; the `client` and `server` labels are application-level roles and impose no wire-layer restriction (this is how LSP `$/`reverse requests and ACP `permission/request` work, see D-008).

# Examples ``` use zhive_proto::{Message, Notification}; let n = Notification::new("session/cancel", None); let bytes = serde_json::to_vec(&Message::Notification(n)).unwrap(); assert!(bytes.starts_with(b"{")); ```

anyOf.description: Carries a method invocation expecting a paired [`Response`].
Carries the outcome of a previously sent [`Request`].
Fire-and-forget event, no response is sent or expected.

code.description: Numeric error code; -32700 to -32600 are reserved by spec.

Id.description: JSON-RPC `id` field; numbers, strings and `null` are all valid per spec.

anyOf.description: 64-bit signed integer; covers all real-world client counters.
Opaque string; used by clients that prefer UUIDs.
JSON `null`; permitted by spec but discouraged.

Notification.description: JSON-RPC notification: method + params, no id, no response.

params.description: Method parameters; serde omits the field when `None`.

Request.description:
JSON-RPC request: method + params + correlatable id.

`id` is required by spec; use [`Notification`] instead for fire-and-forget calls.

id.description: Correlation id; the [`Response`] echoes the same value.

jsonrpc.description: Always the literal string `"2.0"`. Enforced on deserialize.

params.description: Method parameters; serde omits the field when `None`.

Response.description: JSON-RPC response: either `result` or `error`, never both.

oneOf.description: Successful outcome with a free-form JSON payload.
Failure outcome carrying a structured error object.

id.description: Correlation id echoed from the matching [`Request`].
